Federal Judge Mark Pittman is seeking to learn about any agreements that may have led to a Musk-owned company's withdrawal of antitrust claims against Apple. Here are the details.

Judge seeks access to any agreements with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a voluntary motion with the court to dismiss their claims against Apple in last year's lawsuit against Apple and OpenAI, with prejudice.

According to the original complaint, Apple and OpenAI were accused of conspiring to prevent competing AI apps from gaining exposure on the App Store through an agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence. Both Apple and OpenAI have denied these claims.

In filings earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI stated only that they had "resolved the claims against Apple in this case" and emphasized that they were not seeking to dismiss claims against OpenAI.

As first reported by POLITICO, Judge Mark Pittman, who has been presiding over the case, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to provide the court with "any agreement or package of agreements with Apple that resolved plaintiffs' claims against Apple in this case."

The order comes in response to an emergency motion from OpenAI, which sought to compel X and SpaceXAI to turn over their agreement with Apple settling the dispute. Pittman also ordered the two companies to respond to OpenAI's motion by noon on September 17.
